reason: Conversation 1 gives an accurate, honest picture from the outset (overload tripping on a failed start; relay vs tired compressor both kept in play, compressor repair flagged as uneconomic at 10 years), asks the two most useful questions, and lays out a sensible safe sequence: unplugged condenser clean and ventilation first, then a cheap relay swap or engineer current-draw test, plus food-safety advice. Conversation 2 reaches the right escalation eventually but is less efficient and less careful: it pushes the user toward pulling the relay and running multimeter tests with vague instructions ('look for a low resistance reading') despite the user saying they weren't confident, implies a visually fine relay means the compressor is at fault, and wastes a turn suggesting a pointless 24-hour wait after the user had already observed a month. Both stay within the safety boundary, but Conversation 1 is clearer, more honest about the relay-vs-compressor uncertainty, and better at repair-vs-replace guidance.
